title: Predicting Internal Control Over Financial Reporting Quality
estimand: Firm-year likelihood of a material weakness in ICFR (I-score).
evidence_verified: Publisher abstract states I-score measures likely presence of a material weakness and predicts MWs and restatements.
Publisher data-availability statement says supporting data come from third-party providers and require paid subscriptions.
blockers: Full fitted model coefficient/intercept vector was not available in the accessible publisher text during this run.
Publisher explicitly states underlying data require paid third-party subscriptions.
decision: Do not freeze as public-only M1; retain as high-priority scientific/model-bank benchmark and source for modern MW-prediction design.

companion_candidate.title: Where's the risk? Material weakness detection in advance of financial misstatement discovery
companion_candidate.decision: Not M1. Preserve for account-level risk / audit-attention module because it explicitly distinguishes financial-statement and account-type risk.
verified_findings: Income-statement MWs are detected in advance more often than balance-sheet MWs; cash-flow-statement MWs less often.
Revenue and asset areas show higher advance MW detection; equity and expense areas lower.
Research design depends on Audit Analytics and Compustat and therefore is not a clean SEC-only M1.

m1_search_rule_after_run: Continue FT50/ABS4 search for a direct MW-existence model with a complete published coefficient vector and inputs reconstructible from public SEC data. If none exists, formally separate exact-literature benchmark from SEC-native public POC rather than silently substituting variables.
